title: 以前, 以后, 后来 and more time words
explain: 以前 means 'before' and 以后 means 'after'. They come after a time or a verb: 八点以前 'before eight'; 睡觉以前 'before going to bed'; 吃饭以后 'after eating'. On their own they also mean 'in the past' and 'later, in the future'.
后来 means 'afterwards' and is only used about the past: 他以前不喝咖啡，后来喝了 'He did not drink coffee before; later he did'. For the future use 以后: 以后我想去中国.
然后 means 'then, after that', the next step in a series (past or future). 最后 means 'finally, last': 最后一个问题.
More time words: 前天 'the day before yesterday', 后天 'the day after tomorrow', 前年 'the year before last', 后年 'the year after next', 最近 'recently'.

examples.en: I must arrive before eight.

examples.zh: 睡觉以前，他喜欢听音乐。
examples.en: Before going to bed, he likes listening to music.

examples.zh: 他以前不喝咖啡，后来喝了。
examples.en: He did not drink coffee before; later he did.
I saw him the day before yesterday.

mistakes: 后来 is only for the past. For the future say 以后: 以后我想去中国, not 后来我想去中国.
以前 and 以后 come after the time or verb: 八点以前, not 以前八点.

q.en: I must arrive before eight.
q.explain: Time + 以前.

q.en: After eating, we go for a walk.
q.explain: Verb + 以后.

q.zh: 睡觉以前，他喜欢听音乐。
q.en: Before going to bed, he likes listening to music.
q.explain: 以前 means before.

q.zh: 他以前不喝咖啡，后来喝了。
q.en: He did not drink coffee before; later he did.
q.explain: 后来 is for the past.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I want to go to China in the future?
q.en: I want to go to China in the future.
q.explain: 以后 can look to the future; 后来 cannot.

title: 应该, 必须, 需要, 不用 and 最好
explain: 应该 (or 该) means 'should': 你应该多休息 'You should rest more'. The negative is 不应该.

必须 means 'must, have to': 学生必须在八点以前到学校 'Students must be at school before eight'. Do not say 不必须. The opposite of 必须 is 不用, 'no need to': 你不用急，慢慢来 'There is no need to rush; take your time'. Do not mix 不用 up with 别, which means 'don't': 别急 'Don't rush'.
需要 is a verb that means 'need': 我需要你的帮助 'I need your help'. It can also be followed by a verb: 你需要多休息.
最好 means 'had better': 外面很冷，你最好多穿一点儿 'It is cold outside, so you had better wear a bit more'.

examples.en: You should rest more.

examples.zh: 学生必须在八点以前到学校。
examples.en: Students must be at school before eight.
There is no need to rush; take your time.

examples.zh: 外面很冷，你最好多穿一点儿。
examples.en: It is cold outside, so you had better wear a bit more.

mistakes: Do not say 不必须. The opposite of 必须 is 不用: 你不用来, not 你不必须来.
应该 and 该 both mean should. 该 is shorter and more common in speech.

q.en: You should rest more.
q.explain: 应该 + verb.

q.en: You do not need to rush.
q.explain: 不用 means no need to.

q.en: I need your help.
q.explain: 需要 means need.

q.zh: 外面很冷，你最好多穿一点儿。
q.en: It is cold outside, so you had better wear a bit more.
q.explain: 最好 means had better.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: You must come at eight?
q.en: You must come at eight.
q.explain: 必须 means must.

title: 只, 只是 and 只能: only
explain: 只 before a verb means 'only': 我只喝水 'I only drink water'; 他只会说汉语 'He can only speak Chinese'. It goes right before the verb.
只是 means 'just, merely': 我只是想帮你 'I just want to help you'; 这只是一个小问题 'This is only a small problem'.
只能 means 'can only, have no choice but to': 没有别的办法，我们只能等 'There is no other way; we can only wait'.
Do not confuse the 'only' 只 (zhǐ) with the measure word 只 (zhī) in 一只猫.

examples.en: I only drink water.
He can only speak Chinese.
I just want to help you.

examples.zh: 没有别的办法，我们只能等。
examples.en: There is no other way; we can only wait.

mistakes: 只 goes right before the verb: 我只喝水, not 我喝只水.
只有 is a different word: it needs 才 in the next part (see 只要 and 只有).

q.en: I only drink water.
q.explain: 只 goes before the verb.

q.en: He can only speak Chinese.
q.explain: 只 + 会 + verb.

q.en: I just want to help you.
q.explain: 只是 means just.

q.en: There are no cars, so we can only walk.
q.explain: 只能 means can only.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I am just asking?
q.en: I am just asking.
q.explain: 只是 comes before the verb.

title: 好像, 看起来, 大概, 其实 and 当然
explain: 好像 means 'it seems, as if': 他好像不在家 'He does not seem to be at home'. 看起来 means 'it looks like': 这个菜看起来很好吃 'This dish looks delicious'. 看来 means 'it seems (from what I can see)': 看来明天要下雨 'It seems it will rain tomorrow'.
大概 means 'probably, roughly': 现在大概九点了 'It is probably about nine now'.
其实 means 'actually, in fact' and points out how things really are, often against what people think: 其实我不是老师 'Actually, I am not a teacher'.
当然 means 'of course': 你会游泳吗？——我当然会 'Can you swim? Of course I can'.

examples.en: He does not seem to be at home.
This dish looks delicious.
It is probably about nine now.
Actually, I am not a teacher.

mistakes: 好像 here means 'seems', not 'like'. For 'like' (be fond of) use 喜欢.
其实 points to the real situation, so it often goes against what was just said. Do not use it just to agree.

q.en: He does not seem to be at home.
q.explain: 好像 goes before the part that seems true.

q.en: This dish looks delicious.
q.explain: 看起来 + description.

q.en: It is probably about nine now.
q.explain: 大概 means probably.

q.en: Actually, I am not a teacher.
q.explain: 其实 means actually.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Of course I can swim?
q.en: Of course I can swim.
q.explain: 当然 goes before the verb.

title: 终于, 几乎, 突然, 马上 and 一定
explain: 终于 means 'at last, finally' and is for something you waited for: 火车终于来了 'The train has finally come'. 几乎 means 'almost, nearly': 我几乎忘了他的名字 'I almost forgot his name'; 几乎没 means 'hardly any': 他几乎没吃东西.
突然 means 'suddenly': 突然，他笑了 'Suddenly, he laughed'; 突然下雨了 'It suddenly started to rain'. It can go before the subject or before the verb.
马上 means 'right away': 我马上就到 'I will be there right away'. 一定 means 'certainly, must': 我一定会给你打电话 'I will definitely call you'.
All of these go right before the verb; 突然 can also start the sentence.

examples.en: The train has finally come.
I almost forgot his name.
Suddenly, he laughed.
I will definitely call you.

mistakes: Use 终于 only for a result you were waiting for. For a surprise, say 突然.
Put these words before the verb: 我马上就到, not 我到马上.

q.en: The train has finally come.
q.explain: 终于 goes before the verb.

q.en: He suddenly laughed.
q.explain: 突然 goes before the verb.

q.en: I almost forgot his name.
q.explain: 几乎 means almost.

q.en: I will be there right away.
q.explain: 马上 means right away.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I will definitely call you?
q.en: I will definitely call you.
q.explain: 一定 goes before the verb.

title: Question words for "any" and "some": 谁都, 想吃什么就吃什么, 在哪儿见过
explain: A question word + 都 or 也 means 'every' or 'any': 谁都知道这件事 'Everyone knows about this'; 我哪儿都不想去 'I don't want to go anywhere'. With 不 or 没 it means 'nothing, nobody, nowhere': 我什么都没买 'I did not buy anything'.
想 + question word + 就 + the same question word means 'as you like': 你想吃什么就吃什么 'Eat whatever you want'; 你想去哪儿就去哪儿 'Go wherever you want'.
一 + measure word + noun + 也 or 都 + 不 or 没 + verb means 'not even one': 教室里一个人也没有 'There is not a single person in the classroom'; 我一个字也不认识 'I do not know a single character'.

A question word can also mean 'some-' when it is not the thing you ask about: 我好像在哪儿见过她 'I think I have seen her somewhere'; 我想给他买一点儿什么 'I want to buy him something'. In a question that ends with 吗, the question word means 'something, anywhere': 你想吃一点儿什么吗？ 'Would you like something to eat?'.

examples.en: Everyone knows about this.
I did not buy anything.
Eat whatever you want.
There is not a single person in the classroom.
I think I have seen her somewhere.
Would you like something to eat?

mistakes: Do not leave out 都 or 也: 谁知道这件事？ is a question 'Who knows?', but 谁都知道这件事 is a statement 'Everyone knows'.
In 想…就… use the same question word twice: 想吃什么就吃什么.
With 吗 at the end, 什么 means 'something': 你想喝一点儿什么吗？ 'Would you like something to drink?'; without 吗 it is a real question: 你想喝什么？ 'What would you like to drink?'.

q.en: Everyone knows.
q.explain: Question word + 都 + verb.

q.en: I do not want to eat anything.
q.explain: Question word + 都 + 不 + verb.

q.en: Eat whatever you want.
q.explain: 想…就… repeats the question word.

q.en: I do not want to go anywhere.
q.explain: 哪儿 + 都 means anywhere.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: There is not a single person here?
q.en: There is not a single person here.
q.explain: 一…也没有 means not even one.

q.en: I think I have seen her somewhere.
q.explain: 哪儿 here means "somewhere"; it is not a question.

q.prompt: Which sentence asks: Would you like something to drink?
q.en: Would you like something to drink?
q.explain: With 吗, 什么 means "something". Without it, you ask "what?".

title: 半, 两三个 and 以上 / 以下
explain: 半 means 'half'. After a measure word: 一个半小时 'one and a half hours'. Before a measure word: 半个小时 'half an hour'; 半年 'half a year'.
Two numbers next to each other (smaller first) mean 'about': 两三个学生 'two or three students'; 我在这里住了七八天 'I stayed here for seven or eight days'.
以上 means 'above, and over' and counts the number itself: 十八岁以上的人 'people aged eighteen and over'. 以下 means 'below, under': 五十块以下的鞋 'shoes under fifty yuan'.

examples.en: I waited for an hour and a half.
He will be here in half an hour.
There are two or three students here.
Shoes under fifty yuan are rare.

mistakes: 半 goes before the measure word in 半个小时 but after it in 一个半小时. Do not say 一半个小时.
Put the smaller number first: 两三个, not 三两个.

q.en: I waited for an hour and a half.
q.explain: Number + measure word + 半 + noun.

q.en: There are two or three students here.
q.explain: Two numbers side by side mean about.

q.en: He will arrive in half an hour.
q.explain: 半个 means half.

q.zh: 十八岁以上的人可以进去。
q.en: People aged eighteen and over can go in.
q.explain: 以上 means and over.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I stayed here for seven or eight days?
q.en: I stayed here for seven or eight days.
q.explain: Put the smaller number first.

title: Words you know, with a new meaning
explain: Some words you already know come back in HSK 3 with another meaning or another sound. The character is the same; the word around it tells you which one it is.
得 děi means 'must, have to' before a verb: 我得走了 'I have to go now'; 你得多休息 'You must rest more'. It sounds different from the 得 after a verb (他跑得很快, de), and from 得 dé 'to get' (得到, 得分).
地 dì means 'ground, place': 地方 'place', 地铁 'subway', 地图 'map', 地上 'on the ground'. It is de only after an adverb (高兴地说). 过去 is also 'the past': 过去的事 'things of the past'.

还 huán means 'to give back': 还书 'return a book', 还钱 'pay back', 还给 'give back to'. 还 hái 'still, also' is the one you already know. 会 huì also means 'a meeting': 开会 'have a meeting'. 长 zhǎng means 'to grow': 长大 'grow up', 长高 'grow taller'; 长 cháng is 'long'.

examples.en: I have to go now.
I have given the book back to him.
We have a meeting tomorrow.
The child has grown up.

mistakes: Do not mix up the sounds: 我得走了 is děi (must), 他跑得很快 is de (how). The characters are the same, the sound is decided by the words around.
还 hái 'still' goes before another verb: 我还没吃 'I have not eaten yet'. 还 huán 'give back' is the verb itself: 还书 'return a book'.

q.en: I have to go now.
q.explain: 得 děi + verb.

q.en: You must rest more.
q.explain: 得 děi + verb.

q.en: The child has grown up.
q.explain: 长大 is zhǎngdà, to grow up.

q.en: I have given the book back to him.
q.explain: 还给 is huán gěi, give back to.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: We have a meeting tomorrow?
q.en: We have a meeting tomorrow.
q.explain: 开会 means to have a meeting.

title: Showing what you think: 不是…吗？, 是…的 and …什么啊
explain: 不是…吗？ is not a real question. It reminds someone of something you both know, often with surprise: 你不是写完作业了吗？ 'Didn't you say you had finished your homework?'; 你不是会说汉语吗？ 'You can speak Chinese, can't you?'. The answer it expects is 'yes'.
是…的 around a description makes it a firm view, like 'really is': 这个问题其实是很简单的 'This problem really is simple'; 他是会来的 'He will come, I am sure'.

A verb or adjective + 什么(啊) pushes back: 'what is there to …?'. 难过什么啊 'What is there to be sad about?'; 你着急什么啊？ 'What are you in such a hurry for?'. It is friendly between people who know each other, but can sound rude to strangers or older people.

examples.en: Didn't you say you had finished your homework?

examples.zh: 这个问题其实是很简单的。
examples.en: This problem really is simple.

examples.zh: 难过什么啊？你的成绩不是挺好的吗？
examples.en: What is there to be sad about? Your grades are pretty good, aren't they?
What are you in such a hurry for?

mistakes: 不是…吗？ expects 'yes': 你不是去过中国吗？ means 'You have been to China, haven't you?'.
Use …什么啊 with friends; with strangers it can sound rude.

q.en: Didn't you say you had finished your homework?
q.explain: 不是 … 吗？ reminds someone of what you both know.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: You can speak Chinese, can't you?
q.en: You can speak Chinese, can't you?
q.explain: The plain question just asks; 不是…吗？ expects "yes".

q.zh: 这个问题其实是很简单的。
q.en: This problem really is simple.
q.explain: 是 … 的 around a description makes it firm.

q.en: What are you in such a hurry for?
q.explain: Adjective + 什么(啊): what is there to …?

q.prompt: Which sentence says: What is there to cry about? You are doing well.
q.en: What is there to cry about? You are doing well.
q.explain: Verb + 什么啊 pushes back.

title: Doubling: 个个, 一天一天 and 不大不小
explain: A measure word said twice means 'every single one': 这些苹果个个都很大 'Every one of these apples is big'; 他的照片张张都很好看 'Every one of his photos is good-looking'. It comes after the noun and usually goes with 都.

一 + measure word + 一 + measure word means 'one by one, step by step', with 地 before the verb: 请一个一个地进来 'Please come in one at a time'; 我的汉语一天一天地好起来了 'My Chinese is getting better day by day'; 一点一点地 'little by little'.
不A不B with two opposite adjectives means 'just right, neither too … nor too …': 这件衣服不大不小 'This top is neither too big nor too small'; 今天不冷不热 'Today is neither cold nor hot'.

examples.en: Every one of these apples is big.
Please come in one at a time.

examples.zh: 我的汉语一天一天地好起来了。
examples.en: My Chinese is getting better day by day.

examples.zh: 这件衣服不大不小，特别合适。
examples.en: This top is neither too big nor too small; it fits really well.

mistakes: Keep 都 after a doubled measure word: 这些苹果个个都很大.
不A不B needs two opposites: 不大不小, 不冷不热, 不早不晚.

q.en: Every one of these apples is big.
q.explain: Noun, then the doubled measure word, then 都.

q.en: Please come in one at a time.
q.explain: 一个一个 + 地 + verb.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: This top is just the right size?
q.en: This top is just the right size.
q.explain: 不A不B needs two opposites: 大 and 小.

q.en: Today is neither cold nor hot.
q.explain: 不 + one adjective, 不 + its opposite.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Every one of his photos is good-looking?
options: 他的照片张张都很好看。
q.zh: 他的照片张张都很好看。
q.en: Every one of his photos is good-looking.
q.explain: Say the measure word twice: 张张.

title: Handy phrases: 看上去, 一般来说, 不一会儿, 不怎么样
explain: 看上去 means 'looks, seems' (from how it looks), like 看起来: 他看上去很累 'He looks tired'; 这个问题看上去很难，其实很简单 'This problem looks hard, but it is actually simple'.
一般来说 means 'generally speaking' and usually starts the sentence: 一般来说，早上锻炼比较好 'Generally speaking, it is better to exercise in the morning'.
不一会儿 means 'before long, a moment later', and the next part usually has 就: 不一会儿，他就来了 'Before long, he arrived'.
不怎么样 means 'not great, so-so', a soft way to say something is not good: 这家饭店的菜不怎么样 'The food at this restaurant is not great'.

examples.en: He looks tired.

examples.zh: 一般来说，早上锻炼比较好。
examples.en: Generally speaking, it is better to exercise in the morning.
Before long, he arrived.

examples.zh: 这家饭店的菜不怎么样。
examples.en: The food at this restaurant is not great.

mistakes: 看上去 is about how something looks; for your opinion use 我觉得.
不一会儿 often goes with 就 in the next part: 不一会儿，他就来了.

q.zh: 这个问题看上去很难，其实很简单。
q.en: This problem looks hard, but it is actually simple.
q.explain: 看上去: looks (from the outside).

q.zh: 一般来说，早上锻炼比较好。
q.en: Generally speaking, it is better to exercise in the morning.
q.explain: 一般来说 starts the sentence.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Before long, he arrived?
q.en: Before long, he arrived.
q.explain: 不 comes before 一会儿.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: The food at this restaurant is not great?
options: 这家饭店的菜不怎么样。
这家饭店的菜怎么样不。
q.zh: 这家饭店的菜不怎么样。
q.en: The food at this restaurant is not great.
q.explain: 不怎么样: not great.

q.en: He looks tired.
q.explain: Person + 看上去 + description.

title: Frames: 从…起, 在…上 and 对…来说
explain: 从 + time + 起 means 'from … on, starting …': 从明天起，我每天早上跑步 'From tomorrow on, I will run every morning'; 从那天起，我们就变成了好朋友 'From that day on, we became good friends'.

在 + area + 上 means 'when it comes to, in terms of': 在学习上，老师给了我很多帮助 'With my studies, my teacher gave me a lot of help'. 在 + noun + 中 means 'in, during': 在生活中，我们会遇到很多问题 'In life, we meet many problems'.
对 + person + 来说 means 'for someone, as far as they are concerned': 对我来说，这个机会非常重要 'For me, this chance is very important'.

examples.zh: 从明天起，我每天早上跑步。
examples.en: From tomorrow on, I will run every morning.

examples.zh: 在学习上，老师给了我很多帮助。
examples.en: With my studies, my teacher gave me a lot of help.

examples.zh: 对我来说，这个机会非常重要。
examples.en: For me, this chance is very important.

examples.zh: 在生活中，我们会遇到很多问题。
examples.en: In life, we will meet many problems.

mistakes: 对…来说 needs both parts: 对我来说, not 对我说 (that means 'say to me').
从…起 needs 起 at the end of the time: 从明天起.

q.zh: 从明天起，我每天早上跑步。
q.en: From tomorrow on, I will run every morning.
q.explain: 从 + time + 起.

q.zh: 对我来说，这个机会非常重要。
q.en: For me, this chance is very important.
q.explain: 对 + person + 来说.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: With my studies, my teacher gave me a lot of help?
options: 在学习上，老师给了我很多帮助。
在学习，老师给了我很多帮助上。
q.zh: 在学习上，老师给了我很多帮助。
q.en: With my studies, my teacher gave me a lot of help.
q.explain: 在 + area + 上 goes at the start.

q.en: For him, Chinese characters are not hard.
q.explain: 对 + person + 来说 at the start.

q.zh: 从那天起，我们就变成了好朋友。
q.en: From that day on, we became good friends.
q.explain: 从 + time + 起.

title: Several describing words before a noun
explain: When several words describe one noun, they all go before it. A common order is: who it belongs to or what was done to it (+ 的), then 这 / 那 + measure word, then the adjective, then the noun: 我昨天买的那条黑色的裤子 'the black trousers I bought yesterday'. The 这 / 那 + measure word part can also come first: 那条我昨天买的裤子.
Short adjectives such as 新, 大 and 小 join the noun without 的: 我的新手机 'my new phone'; 一个大蛋糕 'a big cake'.
Keep the measure word right after 这, 那 or the number: 那条黑色的裤子.

examples.zh: 我昨天买的那条裤子在哪儿？
examples.en: Where are the trousers I bought yesterday?

examples.zh: 这是我妈妈做的一个大蛋糕。
examples.en: This is a big cake my mom made.

examples.zh: 那个穿红色衣服的女孩儿是谁？
examples.en: Who is that girl in red?
My new phone is expensive.

mistakes: The measure word stays with 这 / 那: 那条黑色的裤子, not 那黑色的条裤子.
Everything that describes the noun goes before it: 穿红色衣服的女孩儿 'the girl in red'.

q.zh: 我昨天买的那条裤子在哪儿？
q.en: Where are the trousers I bought yesterday?
q.explain: What was done to it + 的, then 那条, then the noun.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Who is that girl in red?
options: 那个穿红色衣服的女孩儿是谁？
那个女孩儿穿红色衣服的是谁？
q.zh: 那个穿红色衣服的女孩儿是谁？
q.en: Who is that girl in red?
q.explain: The description comes before the noun.

q.zh: 这是我妈妈做的一个大蛋糕。
q.en: This is a big cake my mom made.
q.explain: Who made it + 的, then 一个大蛋糕.

title: Results: 到, 住, 走 and 上
explain: 到 after a verb means you reached or got what you were after: 买到 'manage to buy', 找到 'find', 看到 'see', 听到 'hear'. 火车票你买到了没有？ 'Did you manage to get the train tickets?'; 我找到我的手机了 'I have found my phone'. The negative uses 没: 我没买到票 'I did not manage to get a ticket'.
住 after a verb means it stays put: 记住 'remember (for good)'. 走 after a verb means away: 拿走 'take away', 飞走 'fly away'.

上 after a verb can mean reaching a goal, often after effort or waiting: 考上大学 'get into university'; 我们终于吃上饭了 'We finally got to eat'; 住上新房子 'get to live in a new home'. 上 can also mark the start of a new state: 爱上 'fall in love with'.

examples.en: Did you manage to get the train tickets?
Please remember this number.
Who took my book away?
He got into university.

mistakes: For 'did not manage to' use 没 + verb + 到: 我没买到票, not 我不买到票.
For getting into a school use 考上: 考上大学.

q.en: I have found my phone.
q.explain: Verb + 到: you got what you were after.

q.en: Please remember this number.
q.explain: 记住: remember for good.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I did not manage to get a ticket?
q.en: I did not manage to get a ticket.
q.explain: Use 没 with a result.

q.en: Who took my book away?
q.explain: Verb + 走: away.

q.en: He got into university.
q.explain: 考上: pass the exam and get in.
